newsitem.title: CZECH REPUBLIC: CZECH TV NOVA MARKET SHARE DIPS, BUT DOMINATES.
newsitem.headline: CZECH TV NOVA MARKET SHARE DIPS, BUT DOMINATES.

text.p: station TV Nova's market share dipped in the third quarter but
it widened its lead over its closest rival, public channel CT1,
a market research report released on Thursday said.
Nova, launched in 1994 and majority-owned by Central
European Media Enterprises Ltd , dipped to 65.0 percent
average viewership in the third quarter from 65.4 percent in
the second, the study by research firms GfK and Median said.
CT1's audience share fell 1.7 percentage points to 24.1
percent in the third quarter, but the second nationwide
commercial station Premiera's share rose to 4.2 percent from
3.3 while public broadcaster CT2 rose to 3.8 percent from 3.5.
The study sampled a cross section of 7,681 respondents
asking them their viewing choices from the previous day.
The public broadcaster lost its monopoly when Nova, whose
parent is led by New York cosmetics heir Ronald Lauder, burst
on Czech screens in February 1994 with a mix of mostly American
serials, action films, and tabloid news programmes.
Nova, post-Communist Europe's first statewide commercial
television broadcaster, posted gross profit of $39 million in
1995, up from $10.3 million in its inaugural year.
Among newspapers, GfK said quality daily Mlada Fronta Dnes
ramians the most read paper with 21 percent share on the market
in averaged over the second and third quarter, with 1.27
million readers, up from 1.26 million in the first six months.
The tabloid Blesk was second with 898,000 readers and a 15
percent share, up from 894,000 and a 14 percent share. The
